text: The session store is a zone-redundant managed Redis service in the ACE subscription with a private endpoint, TLS on, two nodes with automatic failover, no eviction with memory sized at peak concurrent sessions x 8 KB plus 50 percent headroom, a 15-minute sliding idle time to live with no absolute cap, persistence off because no business data is held, and a store loss treated as re-authentication only.
why: The architecture fixes the store's role, its session-only boundary and the 15-minute idle timeout but names no product, tier, placement, availability target, eviction policy, capacity, persistence choice or recovery objective, and the story must provision, size and test the store on Day 1.

confirm: SCB IT infrastructure lead at the platform infrastructure review before wave 0 exit
impact: The tier, the memory, the failover topology and the recovery time appear in the provisioned settings, the capacity test and the runbook; a change to the product or the tier is a re-provision with the same keyspace, credential reference and connection profile, and no business change.

text: The working read of the edge record: one public route per screen tab at /api/recovery/cases/{caseId}/<tab>, one inbox stream at /api/recovery/inbox/stream carried as server-sent events, the session cookie opaque, HttpOnly and Secure with a 15-minute sliding idle and no absolute cap fixed by a source, the gateway publishes no Kafka topic, and the owner services keep object-level authorisation.
why: No source publishes the gateway-bff path table, the push transport or the payment-tab operation, and the route document must be published on Day 1 for the gateway, the ACE front end and the integration harness to start.
read: Paths: /api/recovery/cases/{caseId}, /cases/{caseId}/documents, /cases/{caseId}/notices, /cases/{caseId}/payments, /cases/{caseId}/legal-actions, /api/recovery/me/tasks, /api/recovery/inbox/stream. Push: server-sent events. Cookie: HttpOnly and Secure, 15-minute sliding idle, absolute cap not stated. Session: Redis only, no business data. Topics: none published by the edge. Authorisation: coarse at the edge, object-level with the owner.
confirm: Edge contract review with the solution architect, the ACE front-end team, rwb-payment and rwb-comms
impact: If the read is wrong, the tab paths and the stream change in a v2 route document; no business value, schema or business rule changes.

text: The working read of the runtime: three gateway pods per environment behind the shared App Gateway, the inbox push carried as server-sent events over HTTP/2, the screen model assembled per request with no server-side cache of business data, and the permission cache held in memory with a 5-minute refresh from rwb-access plus event invalidation.
why: No source states the deployment unit, the screen-model field list, the push transport or the gateway and session-store sizing, and the app story cannot be built or tested without a read on each.
read: Topology: three pods per environment behind the shared App Gateway. Push: server-sent events over HTTP/2. Screen model: assembled per request, no server-side cache of business data. Permission cache: in memory per pod, 5-minute periodic refresh from rwb-access plus the three event invalidations, last good copy kept on a failed refresh. Sizing: derived from the 2 s timeout, the bulkhead and the p95 budget, to be confirmed with the Redis session store story.
confirm: Edge design review with the platform team, the ACE front-end team and RWB-PLT-N006-INF
impact: If the read is wrong, the pod count, the cache TTL and the push transport change in the deployment and the app story; no contract of an owner service changes.

text: A dedicated partner gateway in its own DMZ zone fronts rwb-partner only and has no route to gateway-bff, another service, the database, Kafka or Temporal; the FAPI 2.0 Security Profile (final Feb 2025) is enforced with pushed authorisation requests mandatory before every authorisation, access tokens sender-constrained by mTLS to the client certificate, private_key_jwt for a confidential client, 5-minute access tokens and no refresh token for a browser partner; partner identities are federated through the bank's external identity provider with a second factor at sign-in; and client certificates are valid for 12 months, rotated inside an overlap window, with revocation effective on the certificate thumbprint check immediately and on any cached decision within 30 days.
why: The architecture fixes the separate DMZ gateway, the FAPI 2.0 profile and multi-factor partner sign-in, but names no gateway product, no client authentication method, no token lifetime, no external identity provider, no certificate validity or revocation time and no DR objective, and the story must provision, configure and test the edge on Day 1.
read: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 7, 8, 17, 20 and 35 with their notes; Program BRD v4 REQ-ACA-012, REQ-S9-008, NFR-003, NFR-056 and NFR-063; Epic 2 BRD v2 RWB-E2-019
confirm: Security architect at the security design authority review before the penetration test, with SCB IT security and SCB IT infrastructure
impact: The client authentication method, the token lifetime, the certificate validity and the revocation time appear in the authorisation server configuration, the client registry and the conformance tests; a change to any of them is a gateway configuration change re-tested by the conformance suite, with no service code change and no business change.

text: Airflow is the bank-managed enterprise scheduler outside the AKS cluster; one OAuth 2.0 client-credentials service principal per environment calls the owner operations through the shared App Gateway with a 2 s service timeout and a 60 s task timeout, three retries with exponential backoff and jitter, then an alert to the platform on-call rota; the DAG waits for DailyCaseRun by polling its state every 60 s inside a bounded window; the business-date-ready, extract-run and file-window calls are idempotent per business date (and per report or lot) through the Idempotency-Key and a repeat returns the first result; the scheduler holds no database login, produces no Kafka record and reaches no pod directly.
why: Architecture v5 fixes where Airflow sits and what it must do but marks it 'to discuss' and names no product, tenancy, DAG, identity method, retry value, wait mechanism or file-window operation, so the edge cannot be provisioned, tested or handed over without a stated default read.
